items.readable_text:
Content:
The minimum of a set [MATH: S] is the element [MATH: x_{\min} \in S] such that
[MATH: x_{\min} \leq x]
for all [MATH: x \in S.] In other words, the minimum is the element of [MATH: S] that is smaller than or equal to any other element.

Content:
Similarly, the maximum of a set [MATH: S] is the element [MATH: x_{\max} \in S] such that
[MATH: x \leq x_{\max}]
for all [MATH: x \in S.] In other words, the maximum is the element of [MATH: S] that is larger than or equal to any other element.

Content:
For example, what are the minimum and maximum of the following set?

Content:
[MATH: A = \big\{ 2, \: -\sqrt{5}, \: 3, \: -1 \big\}]

Content:
Note that [MATH: -\sqrt{5} \approx -2.236.] Therefore:

Content:
[MATH: min(A)|= min{2, − sqrt(5), 3, − 1} = − sqrt(5); max(A)|= max{2, − sqrt(5), 3, − 1} = 3]

Content:
Some sets may not have a maximum or minimum.

Content:
For example, consider the semi-open interval of real numbers [MATH: B=[1, 5).] In this case, we have

Content:
[MATH: \min(B) = \min[1, 5) = 1.]

Content:
However, since [MATH: 5 \notin B,] the set has no maximum!

Content:
Finally, note the following:

Content:
- The maximum and minimum elements must belong to the underlying set.
- If the maximum or minimum elements exist, they are unique. In other words, there can be, at most, only one maximum and only one minimum.
- If the "less than or equal to" operation is not defined for all elements of a set [MATH: S,] then the set has no maximum or minimum. For example, the following set has no minimum and maximum:
[MATH: S = \big\{\mathbb R, \clubsuit, 2, 3, \langle 1, 2, 3\rangle \big\}]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The minimum of a set [MATH: S] is the element [MATH: x_{\min} \in S] such that
[MATH: x_{\min} \leq x]
for all [MATH: x \in S.] In other words, the minimum is the element of [MATH: S] that is smaller than or equal to any other element.

Content:
Similarly, the maximum of a set [MATH: S] is the element [MATH: x_{\max} \in S] such that
[MATH: x \leq x_{\max}]
for all [MATH: x \in S.] In other words, the maximum is the element of [MATH: S] that is larger than or equal to any other element.

Content:
For example, what are the minimum and maximum of the following set?

Content:
[MATH: A = \big\{ 2, \: -\sqrt{5}, \: 3, \: -1 \big\}]

Content:
Note that [MATH: -\sqrt{5} \approx -2.236.] Therefore:

Content:
[MATH: min(A)|= min{2, − sqrt(5), 3, − 1} = − sqrt(5); max(A)|= max{2, − sqrt(5), 3, − 1} = 3]

Content:
Some sets may not have a maximum or minimum.

Content:
For example, consider the semi-open interval of real numbers [MATH: B=[1, 5).] In this case, we have

Content:
[MATH: \min(B) = \min[1, 5) = 1.]

Content:
However, since [MATH: 5 \notin B,] the set has no maximum!

Content:
Finally, note the following:

Content:
- The maximum and minimum elements must belong to the underlying set.
- If the maximum or minimum elements exist, they are unique. In other words, there can be, at most, only one maximum and only one minimum.
- If the "less than or equal to" operation is not defined for all elements of a set [MATH: S,] then the set has no maximum or minimum. For example, the following set has no minimum and maximum:
[MATH: S = \big\{\mathbb R, \clubsuit, 2, 3, \langle 1, 2, 3\rangle \big\}]

---

Item 2 — Example: Finding the Maximum and Minimum of a Set

Example Prompt:
What are the minimum and maximum of the set [MATH: A = \left[0,3\right]?]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Recall that

- [MATH: x_{\max}] is the maximum of a set [MATH: S] if [MATH: x_{\max} \in S] and [MATH: x \leq x_{\max}] for all [MATH: x \in S,] and
- [MATH: x_{\min}] is the minimum of a set [MATH: S] if [MATH: x_{\min} \in S] and [MATH: x_{\min} \leq x] for all [MATH: x \in S.]

Therefore, we have the following:
[MATH: min(A)|= min[0, 3] = 0; max(A)|= max[0, 3] = 3]
